title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp. 43-46. S is a set with a topology tau. T is a subset of S, presumably closed, and U = S \ T is open. On T there is a second topology tau_0 that is finer than tau|T. The topology tau' on S is obtained by gluing: it keeps tau on the U-part and uses tau_0 on T. It is characterised by the closure formula from the margin of p.43/44: for every X in S, closure_{tau'}(X) = closure_tau(X ∩ U) ∪ closure_{tau_0}(X ∩ T). In particular tau' is finer than tau.

The page states a corollary, labelled 'Variante plus restreinte au cas des ensembles topologiques', i.e. the ordinary topological case as opposed to the 'ultratopological' (poset/Alexandrov-type) case treated on p.46. Corollary: a subset A of S is tau-closed if and only if (a) A is tau'-closed and (b) its trace A ∩ T is closed for tau|T. The added line reformulates this: tau is the final topology on S for the two maps id: (S,tau') -> S and i: (T, tau|T) -> S. Necessity is obvious.

Sufficiency, as finally written (an earlier crossed-out argument via X_U and X_B is abandoned):
- Since X is tau'-closed, X equals its tau'-closure, which by the formula is closure_tau(X ∩ U) ∪ closure_{tau_0}(X ∩ T).
- X ∩ T is tau|T-closed, hence tau_0-closed because tau_0 is finer, so the second term is just X ∩ T.
- Hence X = closure_tau(X ∩ U) ∪ (X ∩ T), a union of two tau-closed sets, so X is tau-closed.

Purpose: this is one step in a comparison between a space and its modification (refinement) along a closed stratum. Such a modification is a recollement of the open part with a re-topologised closed part. The next page uses the analogous statements in the 'ultratopological' (Alexandrov/poset) case to prove homotopy-equivalence criteria of Quillen Theorem A type (fibres phi*^{-1}(J_{<=x}) weakly contractible imply an isomorphism).
errors: The last step (X ∩ T tau|T-closed implies X ∩ T tau-closed in S) needs T to be tau-closed in S. This is presumably part of the standing hypotheses (U open, T its complement) but is not restated here.
Notation drifts: A becomes X in the proof; T is called B in the crossed-out X_B; the script U and T are used interchangeably with tau.
The cross-reference reads 'page 43, marge', but in the supplied transcription the formula appears in the margin of p.44. It may originally be on p.43; this is minor.
The first proof attempt (via X_U = X ∩ U being closed for tau|U) is crossed out. It is muddled and was rightly abandoned for the closure-formula argument.

ideas.what: Gluing a topology on S from an open part U (keeping tau) and a closed part T (with a finer topology tau_0), characterised by the closure formula closure_{tau'}(X) = closure_tau(X ∩ U) ∪ closure_{tau_0}(X ∩ T)
ideas.modern_name: recollement / gluing of topologies along an open-closed decomposition; modification of a topology along a closed stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Recollement of topoi: Artin, Grothendieck, Verdier (SGA 4); the point-set version is folklore
ideas.where_published: Recollement of topoi along open/closed subtopoi in SGA 4 (exposé IV); the specific point-set refinement construction is not, to my knowledge, published by him

ideas.what: Corollary: the original topology tau is the final topology for id: (S,tau') -> S and the inclusion (T, tau|T) -> S, i.e. A is closed iff it is tau'-closed and its trace on T is closed
ideas.modern_name: final (coinduced) topology; recovering a coarser topology from a refinement plus a trace

missed.claim: The page belongs to an apparently unpublished 1986 development, 'Algèbre des figures', with a parallel 'ensembles topologiques' / 'ultratopologiques' (Alexandrov/poset-like) theory. It is used on the next page for Quillen-Theorem-A-type criteria. The page itself is routine point-set topology. Only the surrounding programme (topology refinements along strata compared with homotopy types of posets) might be of historical interest, and it is not established on this page.
missed.quote: Variante plus restreinte au cas ensembles topologiques ... la top. tau sur S est finale pour S -id-> S, T -i-> S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of Grothendieck's mid-1980s 'tame topology' / combinatorial-figure work, linking to finite-space homotopy theory (McCord, Stong). It contains no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary and correct general-topology lemma (characterising closed sets of a topology via a refinement plus the trace on a closed subset, i.e. a final topology). It is standard; interest is only contextual, within the unpublished 'Algèbre des figures' programme.
transcription_corrections: 'la top. tau sur S est fixée par' should most likely read 'la top. tau sur S est finale pour (S -id-> S, T -i-> S)'. This matches the mathematics: tau is the final topology for these two maps.
The first line 'en remarquant [-dans-] le infra. tiers initial[?]' is largely illegible. It may be something like 'en reprenant dans le cadre ... initial'; the transcription is unreliable.
The bracketed line under 'Corollaire' is most likely 'Variante plus restreinte au cas des ensembles topologiques' rather than 'Variante plus de restreindre'.
The margin note read as 'interprétation initiale' is likely 'Interprétation finale' (or 'initiale'), referring to the final-topology reformulation.
'X_B' in the crossed-out passage denotes X ∩ T: B and T are used for the same closed part.
The final line reads '... fermé comme réunion de deux fermés', which the transcription has correctly in substance.
